title: Redirects can bypass the SSRF validation on the article source fetch
reasoning: The route is described as SSRF-safe and validates only the stored article URL before issuing the request. The HTTP client follows redirects automatically, but there is no validation of each redirect target or the final response URL. A public article URL that redirects to localhost, a link-local metadata endpoint, or another private address can therefore turn this API route into an authenticated server-side request to internal network resources.
reproduction: Create a DigestArticle whose URL points to a public HTTP endpoint that returns a 302 Location header for http://127.0.0.1:<internal-port>/, then call GET /{digest_id}/articles/{article_id}/source. The initial URL passes validate_public_url, and httpx follows the private redirect because no per-redirect validation is performed.
recommendation: Disable automatic redirects and manually follow them only after running validate_public_url on every Location target, or add an httpx redirect hook/custom transport that rejects non-public redirect destinations before connecting. Also validate the final URL before returning it.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests reference get_digest_article_source or fetch_html_document redirect behavior, and the existing test suite search found no source-route coverage.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an async test for fetch_html_document or the route that serves a public-looking URL returning a redirect to 127.0.0.1 and asserts the request is rejected before connecting to the private target.
minimumFixScope: app/services/reader_service.py redirect handling, plus a focused regression test; the route can keep calling fetch_html_document once the helper enforces redirect-target validation.
